colors.name: color/canvas
colors.description: Surfaces, ink and fills are steps of one gray ramp (`--gray-1` … `--gray-12`, in the base layer), so every neutral in the interface shares one hue. Surfaces sit off the ramp on its hue: white in light, and in dark a lift of about 0.03 per height above the canvas.

colors.name: color/well
colors.description: Below the surface: the track of a segmented control, a tab row or a switch, and a sunk state. The fill in light; in dark a step under the canvas, so the key on it is the lighter part.

colors.name: color/field
colors.description: The ground of a text field: white in light, the canvas in dark, so it reads as an opening in a card.

colors.name: color/knob
colors.description: The switch knob, off and on: white in light, and in dark mid grey on the well and near white on the brand.

colors.name: color/knob-on
colors.description: The switch knob, off and on: white in light, and in dark mid grey on the well and near white on the brand.

colors.name: color/ink-inverse
colors.description: The ink on a solid ink fill: a primary button, a tooltip, a checked neutral control.

colors.name: color/fill-subtle
colors.description: Hover, selected and the code block, pressed. Opaque, so a fill reads the same anywhere and rows slide under a sticky one.

colors.name: color/fill
colors.description: Hover, selected and the code block, pressed. Opaque, so a fill reads the same anywhere and rows slide under a sticky one.

colors.name: color/fill-strong
colors.description: Hover, selected and the code block, pressed. Opaque, so a fill reads the same anywhere and rows slide under a sticky one.

colors.name: color/edge-subtle
colors.description: Hairlines. Every 1px outline is a `border` in one of these; `border` alone draws `edge`. Each is the ink in light and white in dark at a fraction, so a hairline takes its tone from what it sits on: a card, the canvas, a fill or a tinted callout. Two bordered boxes must not overlap, or the shared line doubles. The strength follows the role: `edge-subtle` a quiet divider, `edge` a card, a dialog or a divider, `edge-strong` anything operated (a field, a button, a raised key, a checkbox), `edge-solid` a control under the pointer, and `edge-float` whatever floats over the page.

colors.name: color/edge-solid
colors.description: The edge of a control under the pointer: one step past the strong edge.

colors.name: color/edge-float
colors.description: The edge of a menu, a select's list, a popover, a tooltip or a toast. In light it is `edge`, since the popup's shadow separates it from the page. In dark it is `edge-strong`: a black shadow barely shows on the dark page, and the popup's lighter surface weakens a translucent line, so the edge has to carry the separation alone.

colors.name: color/scrim
colors.description: The page behind a dialog or a sheet, unblurred. In light the fill at 80%: the page fades back rather than darkening, so the dialog stays the lightest surface. In dark black at 50%, since a lighter veil would lift the page above the dialog.

colors.name: color/drop

colors.name: gray/1
colors.description: The gray ramp under every neutral token. One hue, chroma rising toward the middle and falling off at both ends, so all twelve steps read as one family; dark keeps its chroma low, so the surfaces read as charcoal rather than coloured. Step 1 is the canvas and step 12 the ink in both themes: 2–4 are fills (hover, selected, pressed, spaced so each reads apart from the next), 5–8 the solid greys behind the translucent edges, 9 muted ink, 10 muted ink under the pointer, 11 secondary ink. Dark ink stops short of white, which glares on the dark canvas. Components never use a step directly; they use the token that names its job.

shadows.name: shadow/control
shadows.description: Depth only. An outline is a `border` in an edge colour, so a state that changes one never restates the other. Anything resting on the page takes the crisp 1px drop and at most one short layer, whose negative spread keeps it under the surface: no long soft blur, which reads as a glow rather than as an object resting on the page. Only what floats over the page, a popup, a dialog or a drawer, adds one faint long layer, so it separates from a busy chart or table beneath it. `control` lifts a button, a checkbox, a radio, a switch's knob or a picker's chosen option, and a press takes it away. `well` is anything sunk into its surface, and light falls from above, so its top edge is the dark one. `card` is a resting panel and `card-hover` a clickable card under the pointer. `popup` holds a menu, select or popover over the page, `tooltip` is the same idea at caption size, `modal` a dialog or bottom sheet, and `drawer` the modal shadow cast sideways.
